channel.title: Libertas - Freedom Tech Signals
channel.description: Curated insights on freedom technology: Bitcoin, privacy tools, censorship resistance, and digital sovereignty.

item.title: WiFi Signals Can Now Identify People Through Radio Wave Analysis
item.description: Researchers demonstrate WiFi sensing technology that identifies individuals by analyzing how WiFi signals interact with their bodies, creating surveillance capabilities from existing infrastructure.

item.title: Bitcoin and Freedom Tech Hub Launches in Nairobi with Infrastructure Focus
item.description: Node NBO opens in Nairobi as Africa's first dedicated Bitcoin/freedom tech co-working space, featuring solar power, satellite internet paid in Bitcoin, and partnerships with HRF and key African Bitcoin companies.

item.title: Iran's 83-Day Internet Blackout Highlights Critical Need for Censorship-Resistant Comms
item.description: Iran has imposed a record-breaking 83-day nationwide internet blackout to hide media crackdowns, creating an information vacuum that demonstrates the urgent need for mesh networks and satellite communications.

item.title: Iran Internet Connectivity Returns After 3-Month Government Blackout
item.description: Internet connectivity is partially returning to Iran after nearly 90 days of government-imposed blackout, though permanence of reconnection remains uncertain.

item.title: Indonesia Plans Government Vetting System for Human Rights Defenders
item.description: Indonesia's government announced plans to create an assessment team to determine who qualifies as a 'genuine' human rights defender, following acid attack on activist Andrie Yunus by soldiers.

item.title: Access Now Fights to Uphold Court Injunction Against NSO Pegasus Targeting WhatsApp
item.description: Access Now filed amicus brief urging Ninth Circuit to maintain permanent injunction preventing NSO Group from targeting WhatsApp users with Pegasus spyware that bypasses encryption protections.

item.title: Treasury Nominee Bessent Reiterates Opposition to CBDC, Pushes Crypto Clarity Act
item.description: Treasury Secretary nominee Scott Bessent reaffirmed opposition to a U.S. central bank digital currency and urged Congress to pass cryptocurrency regulatory clarity legislation.

item.title: Russia Bans 9 LGBT Rights Groups as 'Extremist,' Creating Demand for Secure Comms
item.description: Russian courts banned 9 LGBT support organizations as 'extremist' with up to 12-year prison penalties, forcing groups to seek censorship-resistant tools to continue operations.

item.title: EFF Releases Guide to Combat Digital Surveillance Abuses in the Americas
item.description: EFF published comprehensive guide outlining legal frameworks and institutional safeguards needed to curb systematic digital surveillance abuses across Latin America, leveraging Inter-American human rights law.

item.title: FBI Seeks Nationwide Real-Time License Plate Surveillance Network
item.description: FBI published RFP for contractors to provide near real-time access to license plate readers covering 75% of US locations, creating nationwide vehicle tracking capability.

item.title: JPMorgan CEO Dimon Declares War on Crypto Clarity Act, Attacks Coinbase
item.description: JPMorgan's Jamie Dimon vows to fight the Clarity Act, claiming it lets crypto firms operate like banks without regulatory obligations, while calling Coinbase CEO Armstrong 'full of sh*t'.

item.title: China's New Xinjiang Secrecy Law Embeds AI Surveillance Into Social Governance
item.description: China's new state secrets regulation for Xinjiang uses AI monitoring and grassroots reporting to control information flows, making everyday communication subject to security evaluation and creating a 'structure of silence.'

item.title: EFF Reveals Meta's Strategic Timing for Privacy-Invasive Face Recognition Release
item.description: Internal Meta documents show the company planned to launch face recognition for smart glasses during periods when civil rights groups would be distracted by other political concerns.

item.title: El Salvador Detains Anti-Corruption Lawyer for One Year, Triggers Mass Exodus of Rights Groups
item.description: Salvadoran authorities have held prominent anti-corruption lawyer Ruth López in sealed pretrial detention for one year, sparking wider crackdown that forced 140+ activists and journalists into exile.

item.title: Schneier: Systematic Chilling Effects as Government Strategy Against Dissent
item.description: Bruce Schneier and Jon Penney analyze how surveillance, threats, and abuse of power create systematic chilling effects that suppress dissent and activism, arguing this represents a deliberate strategy rather than incidental government overreach.

item.title: Rights Groups Demand Microsoft Disclose Review of Israeli Military AI/Cloud Services
item.description: Five major rights organizations are pressuring Microsoft to publish findings of its review into Israeli military use of Azure and AI services for surveillance and targeting of Palestinians.

item.title: Venezuelan Mother Dies After 16-Month Search for Secretly Dead Political Prisoner Son
item.description: Carmen Navas, 82, died after learning her son Víctor was secretly dead in state custody for 10 months while she searched for him. Case highlights Venezuela's enforced disappearances of political prisoners.

item.title: Mexican Journalist Targeted with Malware Surveillance Attacks
item.description: Award-winning Mexican journalist Maria Teresa Montaño discovered malware compromise of her devices after investigating corruption, highlighting urgent need for digital security tools in hostile environments.

item.title: How Journalists Navigate Internet Shutdowns Across Iran, India, Ethiopia, and Turkey
item.description: Global Voices report documents how journalists work around government-imposed internet shutdowns and targeted censorship across multiple countries, with Iran's recent blackouts affecting thousands of protesters.

item.title: Trump Orders Fed to Review Crypto Access to U.S. Payment Rails
item.description: Trump signed executive order directing Federal Reserve to audit regulations blocking crypto firms from master accounts and payment rails within 3 months, potentially opening direct access to core U.S. financial infrastructure.

item.title: Gulf States Launch Information Crackdown During Iran War, Target Journalists
item.description: Gulf governments are systematically suppressing information about Iran war attacks, detaining journalists, revoking citizenships, and blocking social media accounts to control what populations can see and share.

item.title: Texas Forms Bitcoin Reserve Committee, Moves to Direct BTC Custody
item.description: Texas announced a 5-member advisory committee for its Strategic Bitcoin Reserve and issued RFP for crypto custodian to transition from ETF exposure to direct Bitcoin custody.

item.title: South Carolina Bans CBDC Payments, Supports Crypto Mining
item.description: South Carolina governor signed legislation banning state entities from accepting CBDCs and providing strong support for cryptocurrency mining operations.

item.title: CPJ Files Brief to Protect Encryption from NSO's Pegasus in WhatsApp Case
item.description: Committee to Protect Journalists and 10 civil society orgs filed amicus brief supporting permanent injunction against NSO Group to protect WhatsApp encryption from Pegasus spyware targeting journalists.

item.title: DRC: Secret Cyber Defense Unit Disappears Dissidents, HRW Documents Network of Detention Sites
item.description: Human Rights Watch documents systematic repression in DRC where National Cyber Defense Council arbitrarily arrests activists, holding them in secret locations without charges or legal access.

item.title: Citizen Lab Exposes Mobile Networks as Covert Surveillance Platforms
item.description: New Citizen Lab research reveals how weaknesses in mobile network technology and governance enable sophisticated surveillance campaigns targeting users.

item.title: EFF Exposes Mass ALPR Mission Creep: School Checks, Employment Screening
item.description: EFF analysis of millions of Flock Safety ALPR searches reveals police using license plate surveillance for school residency verification and employment background checks, far beyond original crime-fighting purpose.

item.title: EFF Warns Age Verification Creates Mass Surveillance Infrastructure
item.description: EFF highlights how age verification mandates force users to submit sensitive personal data to third parties, creating centralized honeypots that have already been breached multiple times.

item.title: CPJ Warns Journalists of Border Surveillance, Device Seizures at 2026 FIFA World Cup
item.description: Committee to Protect Journalists warns 50,000 accredited World Cup journalists may face border questioning, device confiscation, and immigration enforcement targeting their reporting work.

item.title: Tunisia Escalates Media Crackdown with New Journalist Convictions
item.description: Tunisia convicted lawyer-commentator Sonia Dahmani under cybercrime law for criticizing prison conditions, part of systematic repression targeting journalists and blocking protest coverage.

item.title: EFF Highlights End-to-End Encryption Advances in Apple-Android RCS Messaging
item.description: EFF's latest newsletter covers recent progress in encrypted messaging between Apple and Android devices, plus analysis of Canada's surveillance bill and social media restrictions.

item.title: Press Freedom Groups Urge New Guatemala AG to End Journalist Persecution
item.description: Nine international organizations led by CPJ call on Guatemala's new attorney general to stop criminal prosecutions of journalists, with 20+ reporters fled the country in 2022-2023 due to systematic targeting.

item.title: Gulf States Expand Wartime Censorship Laws, Target Journalists for Routine Reporting
item.description: Committee to Protect Journalists documents systematic crackdown on press freedom across Gulf states since Iran war began, with journalists detained for sharing verified public information under vague 'national security' laws.

item.title: Microsoft Fires Israel Chief Over Human Rights Violations in Gaza Surveillance Ops
item.description: Microsoft terminated its Israel Country General Manager after investigations revealed Azure cloud/AI services were used for mass surveillance and military targeting in Gaza, violating company human rights standards.

item.title: Retired Cop Wins $835K Settlement After 37-Day Jail for Trump Meme
item.description: Larry Bushart won $835,000 settlement after Tennessee sheriff jailed him 37 days for posting Trump meme on Facebook, establishing precedent for First Amendment violations.

item.title: Freedom House Links Iran's Internet Blackouts to State Repression Strategy
item.description: Freedom House connects Iran's ongoing internet blackouts and digital repression to broader authoritarian strategy of engineering distrust and fracturing opposition movements.

item.title: US House Whip Pushes Anti-CBDC Act to Block Government Digital Currency
item.description: House Majority Whip Tom Emmer is advocating for his Anti-CBDC Surveillance State Act, which passed the House but awaits Senate action to permanently ban central bank digital currencies.

item.title: Turkish Journalist Arrested Under Disinformation Law for School Weapons Report
item.description: Turkish journalist Yelis Ayaz arrested for reporting on politician's son allegedly bringing weapons to school, highlighting systematic use of disinformation law to prosecute media.

item.title: Canada's Bill C-22 Could Enable US Real-Time Surveillance via CLOUD Act Agreement
item.description: Canada's proposed Bill C-22 would compel tech providers to build surveillance capabilities and enable a CLOUD Act agreement giving US agencies like the FBI power for real-time surveillance including wiretaps in Canada.

item.title: China Pressures Zambia to Cancel Major Digital Rights Conference RightsCon
item.description: Chinese government pressure forced cancellation of RightsCon 2026 in Zambia after officials objected to planned discussions of China's digital authoritarianism and Taiwanese activist participation.

item.title: Russia Drafts 'Civic Death' Law to Cut Digital Services for Exiled Critics
item.description: Russia's parliament reviews draft law denying exiled critics access to digital government services, banking, and consular support - creating urgent need for sovereign identity solutions.

item.title: Kazakhstan Forces Anti-War Orthodox Priest Into Psychiatric Detention
item.description: Kazakhstan authorities transferred activist priest Yakov Vorontsov to psychiatric facility on dubious drug charges, following years of pressure over his anti-war stance and efforts to establish independent Orthodox community.

item.title: Philippine Court Dismisses Terror Financing Charges Against NGO; Bank Accounts Remain Frozen
item.description: A Philippine court dismissed terrorism financing charges against NGO CERNET, but authorities continue weaponizing anti-money laundering laws against civil society despite being removed from FATF grey list.

item.title: Iran Launches Bitcoin-Settled Maritime Insurance for Strait of Hormuz Transit
item.description: Iran launched Hormuz Safe, a Bitcoin-settled maritime insurance platform for Strait of Hormuz shipping, projecting $10B revenue while leveraging Bitcoin's censorship resistance under US sanctions.

item.title: Mexican Journalists Jailed Under New AI Manipulation Laws After Gov Corruption Coverage
item.description: Mexican journalists arrested on charges of 'illegal use of AI' after reporting on governor corruption video that official claimed was deepfaked, highlighting weaponization of AI laws against press.

item.title: Tails 7.8 Fixes Critical Security Vulnerabilities That Could Enable Deanonymization
item.description: Tails 7.8 patches critical Linux kernel vulnerabilities that could allow attackers to gain admin privileges and potentially deanonymize users, while removing pre-installed Thunderbird.

item.title: US Treasury Seizes Nearly $1B in Iranian Crypto Assets
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent disclosed the U.S. has seized nearly $1 billion in cryptocurrency assets from Iran, demonstrating state capacity for large-scale crypto confiscation.

item.title: Rights Groups Demand Microsoft Disclose Review of Azure Services to Israeli Military Surveillance
item.description: Access Now and coalition demand Microsoft publicly release findings of investigation into Azure cloud services used by Israeli military units for mass surveillance and AI-assisted targeting of Palestinians.

item.title: Rights Groups Demand Microsoft Disclose Israeli Military Surveillance Tech Review
item.description: Digital rights coalition demands Microsoft publish findings of its review into Israeli military's use of Azure cloud and AI services for surveillance and targeting of Palestinians.

item.title: Binance Denies WSJ Report on $850M Iran-Linked Transactions
item.description: Binance CEO Richard Teng denied Wall Street Journal allegations that $850 million in Iran-linked transactions flowed through the exchange to the IRGC.

item.title: Maldives Jails First Journalists Since 2008, Escalates Press Freedom Crackdown
item.description: Maldives authorities jailed two journalists for reporting on a gag order, marking the first criminal imprisonment of journalists since the country's 2008 democratic constitution, amid broader media suppression efforts.

item.title: 116K Dark Web Exposures Found for Major US Media Organizations
item.description: Proton's research found over 116,000 dark web exposures tied to NY Times, Washington Post, and WSJ email addresses, including 12,000+ plaintext passwords, creating cybersecurity risks for journalists and sources.

item.title: Bipartisan Amendment Would Ban Police License Plate Tracking Nationwide
item.description: A bipartisan federal highway bill amendment would strip funding from cities and states that operate automated license plate tracking programs, effectively ending mass surveillance via ALPR technology.

item.title: OONI Joins Quadratic Funding Campaign for Internet Freedom Projects
item.description: OONI and 9 other internet freedom projects launched a quadratic funding campaign to secure decentralized funding, citing sustainability risks.

item.title: Access Now Links Privacy Protection to Disinformation Defense in Latin America
item.description: Digital rights org Access Now argues that strict data protection laws are key to reducing disinformation impact, especially during elections in Latin America where microtargeting exploits personal data for political manipulation.

item.title: White House to Announce Strategic Bitcoin Reserve Details After Legal Framework Completion
item.description: U.S. officials say announcement on Strategic Bitcoin Reserve implementation is imminent after clearing legal hurdles for custody of 328,372 BTC held from law enforcement seizures.

item.title: Meta Blocks Human Rights Accounts in Saudi Arabia and UAE
item.description: Meta has reportedly blocked human rights organizations' accounts from reaching audiences in Saudi Arabia and UAE, demonstrating platform-level censorship in authoritarian regions.

item.title: UK Sanctions HTX Exchange Over Alleged Russia Sanction Circumvention
item.description: The UK sanctioned HTX (formerly Huobi Global) crypto exchange, claiming it's being exploited by Russia to bypass existing financial sanctions.

item.title: 116K Dark Web Exposures Found Tied to Major US News Organizations
item.description: Proton's research found over 116,000 dark web exposures linked to NYT, Washington Post, and WSJ employee emails, including 12,000+ plaintext passwords and 61,000+ pieces of PII.

item.title: DRC Drones Target Radio Station in Escalation of Tech-Enabled Media Suppression
item.description: Military drones struck Radio Tuungane twice in DRC's South Kivu province, with militia threatening journalists over coverage of atrocities. Pattern shows weaponization of surveillance tech against independent media.

item.title: NASA Satellites Can Detect GPS Jammers from Space, Raising Privacy Concerns
item.description: NASA satellites originally designed for weather monitoring can now locate GPS jammers within several kilometers, potentially enabling state surveillance of privacy tools used by activists and dissidents.

item.title: South Carolina Enacts Comprehensive Bitcoin Law, Bans State CBDC Use
item.description: South Carolina passed Senate Bill 163 with bipartisan support, protecting Bitcoin self-custody rights, preventing additional crypto taxes, and banning state entities from using CBDCs.

item.title: Freedom House Links Iran's Internet Blackouts to Historical Resistance Patterns
item.description: Freedom House draws parallels between Poland's Solidarity movement and Iran's current struggle, highlighting the regime's use of internet blackouts and digital repression to fracture opposition movements.

item.title: DRC Uses Cyber Defense Council for Secret Detention of Dissidents
item.description: Congo's National Cyber Defense Council is arbitrarily arresting activists and holding them in secret locations without charges, marking return to Kabila-era repression tactics.

item.title: Freedom House Links Iran's Internet Blackouts to Historical Resistance Patterns
item.description: Freedom House draws parallels between Iran's ongoing internet blackouts and Poland's Solidarity movement, highlighting how authoritarian regimes use digital repression to fracture opposition before democratic movements can unify.

item.title: African Govts Spend $2B on AI Surveillance to Target Opposition, Not Crime
item.description: 11 African governments spent over $2 billion on Chinese/Israeli AI surveillance systems strategically placed in opposition areas rather than high-crime zones, creating digital panopticon to suppress dissent before it forms.
